title: Judge grants TRO against SEC, Greg Sankey over fifth-year issue
dek: A federal judge in Dallas issued a temporary restraining order blocking the SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey from overturning an injunction that grants high-school class of 2022 players a fifth year of college eligibility after NFL contract time. The ruling forces the SEC to honor the prior injunction while the conference pursues legislative action through the Protect College Sports Act.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: A Dallas federal judge issued a temporary restraining order blocking the SEC's attempt to circumvent a court ruling granting ex-NFL players an additional year of college eligibility.
bottom_line: The court order blocks the SEC's immediate workaround but does not settle the underlying dispute over ex-NFL players' college eligibility. Watch for Senate action on the Protect College Sports Act and any further court filings as the SEC and player advocates clash over the legislative path forward.
body: A federal judge in Dallas has issued a temporary restraining order blocking the SEC and Commissioner Greg Sankey from overturning an injunction that grants players from the high-school class of 2022 a fifth year of college eligibility after spending time under NFL contract, according to reporting from Yahoo NFL.

The prior injunction allows players who have signed with NFL teams to return to college for an additional year of play. The SEC's effort to create a conference-wide prohibition on recruiting and enrolling those players appears designed to generate political momentum toward passage of the Protect College Sports Act, per Yahoo's reporting. The Senate is expected to return from summer recess soon, with potential for movement on the legislation.

The temporary restraining order prevents the SEC from circumventing the court's prior ruling while the broader legislative battle continues. The ruling forces the conference to honor the existing injunction even as it pursues legislative action that would secure an antitrust exemption for schools and overturn player-favorable eligibility rules.
